props.title: Under Siege

sections.content: **Under Siege** (1992) marked Steven Seagal's peak as an action star, elevating the "Die Hard on a..." formula with maritime mayhem. Like **Die Hard** (1988) before it, the film trapped its hero in a confined space - this time a Navy battleship - against sophisticated terrorists. Director Andrew Davis, who'd later helm **The Fugitive** (1993), brought serious technical polish to what could've been a B-movie throwaway. The film's success spawned numerous copycats like **Speed** (1994) ("Die Hard on a bus") and **Con Air** (1997) ("Die Hard on a plane"). movies.title: Under Siege
movies.slug: Navy SEAL-turned-cook Casey Ryback must single-handedly stop terrorists from hijacking a battleship's nuclear arsenal. Stars Steven Seagal and Tommy Lee Jones.

sections.content: Tommy Lee Jones and Gary Busey deliver memorably unhinged performances as the villains, following the **Die Hard** template of charismatic antagonists established by Alan Rickman. Jones's Strannix, a rogue CIA operative, brings theatrical menace that contrasts perfectly with Seagal's stoic presence. The film's action sequences hold up remarkably well, favoring practical effects and real explosions over the CGI that would soon dominate the genre in films like **True Lies** (1994).

The film represents the commercial peak of director Andrew Davis's action period, between **Above the Law** (1988) and **The Fugitive** (1993). Davis brought a clean, classical style to the proceedings, avoiding the rapid-cut chaos that would later define action cinema post-**The Bourne Identity** (2002). The battleship setting provides unique action possibilities, with Davis making full use of the cramped corridors, missile bays, and deck spaces. sections.content: **Under Siege** helped establish a sub-genre of naval action thrillers, followed by films like **Crimson Tide** (1995) and **Down Periscope** (1996). While submarine films like **The Hunt for Red October** (1990) existed previously, **Under Siege** brought a more visceral, close-quarters combat approach to maritime action. This influence can be seen in later films like **Captain Phillips** (2013) and even **Speed 2: Cruise Control** (1997), though the latter failed to replicate Under Siege's success.
